_comment: REFERENCE ONLY — adapt paths and domains to your environment before copying to ~/.claude/settings.json

permissions._comment_allow: Bash allowlist entries use permission-rule syntax (Bash(...)) — prefix match with trailing *. The tools.bash.allowList field below is deprecated/ineffective; real bash allowlisting is expressed here.
permissions._comment_deny: Neither Edit(~/.codex/**) nor Edit(~/.gemini/**) nor Write(~/.codex/**) nor Write(~/.gemini/**) are denied here. Per the sandbox schema, Edit(...) AND Write(...) deny rules both merge into sandbox filesystem denyWrite. Denying either would block the codex/gemini CLIs from writing their own session/cache files under ~/.codex and ~/.gemini. Credential-file protection is handled by the explicit Read(...) deny rules on auth.json, oauth_creds.json, google_accounts.json, and history/**.

network._comment_allowedDomains: Docker Hub domains enable public image pulls (supply-chain risk). For air-gapped environments, replace with your private registry URL.
network._comment_allowedDomains_2: Cross-family reviewer domains: Codex CLI (chatgpt.com, api.openai.com) and Gemini CLI (oauth2.googleapis.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com, play.googleapis.com). Remove them if you do not use cross-family reviews.

filesystem._comment_filesystem: ~/.gemini and ~/.codex are broadly allowed for read+write so the gemini and codex CLIs can manage their own OAuth tokens, session files, and caches. Credential-file protection is handled by permissions.deny entries for the specific sensitive files (auth.json, oauth_creds.json, google_accounts.json, history/**).

sandbox._comment_restrictedCommands: Exfiltration vectors (curl, wget, nc) are not listed here because network.allowedDomains already restricts outbound connections. If you weaken network isolation, add exfiltration commands to this list.
